action.note: Rewrote module.py with a recursive deep merge per the user contract. Inputs are deep-copied, null patch values remove keys, nested objects merge recursively, lists are replaced, and mismatched JSON types raise ValueError. Next step is to run the tests.
Removed the copy import, which is not on the allowed list. Deep copying is now done by a local _clone helper, so the module uses no imports. Rerunning tests next.

action.message: module.py now implements solve(data) per the user contract using only the standard library, with no imports. It validates that data has object keys base and patch, deep-clones the inputs so they are never mutated, removes keys whose patch value is null (no-op if absent), merges nested objects recursively, replaces lists wholesale, inserts absent keys as-is, and raises ValueError on JSON type mismatches (booleans and numbers differ). Key order follows base, then patch-only keys. The public tests passed 3/3 on candidate hash e9aa23423b47d1d883cffb441620a04f512ed1513450f2fd9cb3a2d6be38bb68. Only the public suite has run; no user tests were submitted.
